pool.title: Virtual Models
pool.emptyText: No virtual model yet. A virtual model is the name employees type in their AI tool; it can front several vendor models for failover. You must create one before employees can call — there is no default group.
pool.routeHint: Employee requests set model to a virtual model name (e.g. company-chat); the gateway picks a healthy member behind it. Virtual models must be created here first — an unknown group name returns 404.
pool.poolNamePlaceholder: e.g. company-chat (employees request models by this name)
pool.noInstancesTip: No instances under this model category. Connect provider models in Access Management first.
pool.categoryLockedHint: A "{type}" model is selected. Only models of the same category can be added — virtual models route by category, so mixing other categories (e.g. image generation, embedding) would never be invoked.
pool.memberWeightTip: Members reference specific model channels; weight determines the probability of being selected (ignored under the consistent-hash strategy).

strategies.ip-hash: Same IP to the same instance

strategyHints.weighted-random: Not sure? Pick this - the system distributes by weight, so instances with a higher weight are picked more often
strategyHints.round-robin: Picks one instance after another, the most even distribution
strategyHints.least-connections: Prefers the instance with the fewest active connections - useful when instance performance differs a lot
strategyHints.ip-hash: The same IP always goes to the same instance - useful when session affinity is required
strategyHints.consistent-hash: The same user always lands on the same instance, with the least impact when instances are added or removed (weight is ignored)

pool.subtitle: The name employees type in their AI tool; several provider models can sit behind it for automatic failover. Quotas and rate limits are configured here.

pool.priceStatusTooltipNone: No member of this group has a unit price; billing counts ¥0
pool.memberWeightDesc: A higher number gives this model more traffic (all default to 1)
pool.explainBodyV2: Staff can only type virtual model names created here (e.g. company-main) in their tools - never raw names like gpt-4o / claude-3-opus. That way quotas and audit logs stay under control. One virtual model can sit on several real models; there are 5 ways to split traffic: Weighted Random (default, recommended), Round Robin, Least Connections (busier machines take more), IP Hash (the same person always reaches the same model), and Consistent Hash (least disruption when instances come and go).
pool.nameFieldPlaceholder: e.g. company-chat (type this exact name in your tool)
pool.nameFieldHelp: This is the name employees type in their AI tool. If you name it company-chat, they type company-chat — they never need to know it runs GPT or Claude behind the scenes.
pool.editDesc: Staff only see the name "{name}"; several real models sit behind it as fallbacks.

pool.memberPrimaryDesc: Used first when it is healthy
pool.memberBackupDesc: Takes over when the one above fails
